sections.history: Tiruvettakkudi lies near Karaikal, reached by the Karaikal–Poraiyar road about 3 km to Varichakudi, then a branch road marked by an ornamental arch. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, in the Karaikal territory of Puducherry (within the Kaveri delta of the Chola country). The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Tirumeniazhagar — also Sundareswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Soundaranayagi (also Santhanayagi) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram keep the form of the Shiva temples of the Karaikal delta.
sections.legends: The sthala purana ties the name Tiru-Vetta-Kudi to Arjuna's penance: to win the Pashupata weapon, Arjuna did tapas, and Shiva came to him as a hunter, a Vedan, testing him before granting his grace. From that form of the lord as the hunter the place takes its name. Shiva is worshipped here as Tirumeniazhagar, the beautiful-bodied lord, with Soundaranayagi beside him.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a delta village shrine. Pilgrims of the Karaikal country include Tiruvettakkudi among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruvettakkudi the pilgrim comes to the shrine of the beautiful-bodied lord. Before Tirumeniazhagar and Soundaranayagi, in the green Karaikal delta, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple, and the memory of the hunter-lord who tested Arjuna and gave him his grace.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvettakkudi lies near Karaikal, about 3 km along the Karaikal–Poraiyar road to Varichakudi, then a signposted branch road. Karaikal is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
